drivingQuestion: At what point does untithed produce become obligated in tithes — only when it sees the front of the house, or already in the courtyard?
outcomeNote: The dispute between R. Yannai and R. Yoḥanan over the point at which produce becomes liable to tithes is left standing without decision.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּדוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים דּוֹרוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנִים. דּוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים עָשׂוּ תּוֹרָתָן קֶבַע וּמְלַאכְתָּן עֲרַאי, זוֹ וָזוֹ נִתְקַיְּימָה בְּיָדָן. דּוֹרוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנִים שֶׁעָשׂוּ מְלַאכְתָּן קֶבַע וְתוֹרָתָן עֲרַאי, זוֹ וָזוֹ לֹא נִתְקַיְּימָה בְּיָדָן.
segments.en: Summarizing these statements, «Rabba bar bar Ḥana said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of» the tanna «Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi El’ai: Come and see that the latter generations are not like the earlier generations;» rather they are their inferiors. «The earlier generations made their Torah permanent and their work occasional,» and «this,» Torah study, «and that,» their work, «were successful for them.» However, «the latter generations who made their work permanent and their Torah occasional, neither this nor that was successful for them.»

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּדוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים דּוֹרוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנִים. דּוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ מַכְנִיסִין פֵּירוֹתֵיהֶן דֶּרֶךְ טְרַקְסְמוֹן כְּדֵי לְחַיְּיבָן בְּמַעֲשֵׂר, דּוֹרוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנִים מַכְנִיסִין פֵּירוֹתֵיהֶן דֶּרֶךְ גַּגּוֹת, דֶּרֶךְ חֲצֵרוֹת, דֶּרֶךְ קַרְפֵּיפוֹת, כְּדֵי לְפׇטְרָן מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: אֵין הַטֶּבֶל מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּמַעֲשֵׂר עַד שֶׁיִּרְאֶה פְּנֵי הַבַּיִת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בִּעַרְתִּי הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִן הַבַּיִת״.
segments.en: Along these lines, «Rabba bar bar Ḥana said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi El’ai: Come and see that the latter generations are not like the earlier generations.» In the «earlier generations,» people «would bring their fruits into their courtyards through the main gate in order to obligate them in tithes.» However, «the latter generations bring their fruits through roofs, through courtyards and through enclosed courtyards,» avoiding the main gate «in order to exempt them from» the mitzva of «tithing. As Rabbi Yannai said: Untithed produce is not obligated in» the mitzva of «tithing until it sees the front of the house» through which people enter and exit, and it is brought into the house that way «as it is stated» in the formula of the confession of the tithes: «“I have removed the consecrated from the house”» (Deuteronomy 26:13), as the obligation to tithe produce whose purpose has not yet been designated takes effect only when it is brought into the house.

segments.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חָצֵר קוֹבַעַת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאָכְלוּ בִשְׁעָרֶיךָ וְשָׂבֵעוּ״.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even» bringing it into the «courtyard determines» its status as having completed the production process and obligates the produce to be tithed, «as it is written» in the confession of the tithes: “And I have given to the Levite, the stranger, the orphan and the widow, «and they shall eat in your gates and be satisfied”» (Deuteronomy 26:12).

moves.summary: Sums up the preceding Torah-and-work dispute: the earlier generations made Torah permanent and work occasional and succeeded at both.
moves.about: the earlier generations made Torah permanent and work occasional, and both succeeded for them

moves.summary: Second statement in the same series: the earlier generations routed produce so as to incur tithes, the later so as to avoid them.
moves.about: the earlier generations brought produce in through the main gate so as to obligate it in tithes

moves.summary: Adduces R. Yannai's rule that explains why the roof-and-courtyard route evades the tithe.
moves.about: why bringing produce in by roofs and courtyards exempts it — tevel becomes liable only on seeing the front of the house

moves.summary: Prooftext: I have removed the consecrated from the house.
moves.about: prooftext that liability to tithes attaches at the house

moves.summary: R. Yoḥanan holds that even the courtyard fixes liability, against R. Yannai.
moves.about: at what point untithed produce becomes obligated in tithes — only on entering the house, or already on entering the courtyard

moves.summary: Prooftext: and they shall eat in your gates and be satisfied.
moves.about: prooftext that the gates, i.e. the courtyard, fix liability
